entity.summary: Omise Holdings-backed centralized cryptocurrency exchange publicly launched in June 2019, restricted operations to withdrawals on 2020-01-30, and closed on 2020-03-15 after its team concluded that growing regulatory complexity and uncertainty made continued operation uneconomic.
entity.notes: GO.Exchange was a separate Omise Holdings subsidiary. Omise Holdings described the exchange as internally incubated from summer 2018 and independent from OmiseGO/OMG Network. Public launch material appeared in June 2019 after an earlier soft-launch period. Malta is recorded as the intended operating/regulatory base: contemporary reporting says Omise had incorporated in Malta and intended to launch GO.Exchange from there, while the exchange later said it abandoned its Maltese licensing effort because increasing regulatory complexity and uncertainty changed the cost/benefit analysis. HEI does not claim that a Maltese exchange license was granted. On 2020-01-30 the venue stopped new customers, deposits and exchange trading but continued withdrawals until the announced terminal deadline of 2020-03-15 23:00 UTC. No hack or enforcement action is inferred.

events.title: GO.Exchange entered public launch
events.description: GO.Exchange publicly presented itself as a newly launched exchange and began a launch promotion after an earlier development and soft-launch period.
events.notes: The public-launch marker uses the GO.Exchange community announcement dated 2019-06-25. Omise Holdings had described a soft-launch path earlier in 2019, so this date is not treated as the beginning of internal development.

events.title: GO.Exchange announced closure and entered withdrawal-only run-off
events.description: GO.Exchange announced that it would close on 2020-03-15 and immediately stopped accepting new customers, deposits and exchange transactions other than withdrawals.
events.notes: The team attributed the decision to increasing regulatory complexity and uncertainty that changed the economics of operating the exchange. This is modeled as a voluntary shutdown rather than a regulatory enforcement event.

events.title: GO.Exchange reached its announced terminal closure date
events.description: The withdrawal run-off ended at the exchange's announced 2020-03-15 terminal deadline, after trading and deposits had already been disabled since January 30.
events.notes: The exact terminal date follows the operator notice as reproduced contemporaneously, together with later inactive-status evidence. No separate post-closure first-party confirmation was recovered in this review.

evidence.title: GO.Exchange community launch post
evidence.notes: GO.Exchange addressed early adopters as a new exchange and described a launch promotion, supporting the public-launch marker.

evidence.title: Omise Holdings Launches GO.Exchange Crypto Trading Platform
evidence.notes: Contemporaneous coverage states that Omise Holdings subsidiary GO.Exchange had launched its cryptocurrency exchange after development since the previous summer.

evidence.title: Omise Holdings: Strategy Update
evidence.notes: Omise Holdings' group CEO describes GO.Exchange as a newly launched subsidiary developing a user-facing digital asset exchange, with internal incubation beginning in summer 2018 and a separate corporate/product mandate from OmiseGO.

evidence.title: OmiseGO’s foremost crypto exchange is shutting down
evidence.notes: Reports the January 30 shutdown announcement, immediate withdrawal-only restriction, March 15 withdrawal deadline, and the team's regulatory-complexity rationale.

evidence.title: OmiseGo-Backed Exchange Shuts Down
evidence.notes: Quotes GO.Exchange's January 30 closure post and reproduces the withdrawal-only schedule and explanation that regulatory complexity and uncertainty changed the cost/benefit of operating the exchange.

evidence.title: GO.Exchange closure notice reproduction
evidence.notes: Reproduces the closure notice stating that GO.Exchange would close operations on March 15, 2020 and that withdrawals would remain available until 23:00 UTC that day. Used for the announced terminal date, not as an independent first-party archive.

evidence.title: GO.Exchange discontinued exchange profile
evidence.notes: Current exchange directory marks GO.Exchange inactive and identifies it as a former centralized spot exchange, supporting terminal status while not independently establishing the exact 2020 closure date.

evidence.title: Start-up to discuss future of blockchain at GAIMOps
evidence.notes: Contemporaneous reporting says Omise had recently incorporated in Malta and intended to launch its retail digital-asset exchange GO.Exchange from there. HEI uses this for historical operating-base context only and does not infer that GO.Exchange obtained a Maltese exchange license.
